hints.title: Non-Zero Component Skipping
hints.text: When multiplying sparse matrices, any zero value in the first matrix contributes nothing to the result row and can be bypassed.

hints.title: Loop Reordering for Sparsity Exploitation
hints.text: Iterate rows of mat1, then intermediate column p. If mat1[i][p] is non-zero, iterate columns j of mat2 and accumulate the product.

hints.title: Three Nested Loops with Guard Condition
hints.text: Allocate an m by n zero matrix. Loop i over m, p over k. If mat1[i][p] is not zero, loop j over n and add mat1[i][p] * mat2[p][j] into result[i][j].

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(M * K * N) worst case time, running substantially faster on sparse inputs.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Standard i-j-k triple nesting performs K operations for every output cell even when most entries are zero.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Loop reordering to i-k-j places the zero check on the outer operand, bypassing the entire inner vector of length N.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize how loop permutation (i-k-j vs i-j-k) enables effective sparsity pruning.
